youtube.title: SARAH MYHILL
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with British physician Dr Sarah Myhill, Medical Ethics Director of the UK Medical Freedom Alliance. Sarah discusses her open letter to Chief Medical Officer Sir Chris Whitty, in which she alleges he failed to uphold medical ethics and informed consent during the Covid response. For more information: Visit Dr Myhill’s website or find her on X and YouTube For her Podcast or to purchase Sarah’s books For more on UK Medical Freedom Alliance

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: With Victoria’s state election approaching, Tim Wilms joins Paul Brennan to examine Labor’s plunging poll numbers, One Nation’s surge and the Liberal Coalition’s prospects of winning government. They also discuss controversy surrounding dis-endorsed candidates, allegations of union influence emerging from the Big Build Royal Commission, and questions over government spending, immigration, puberty blockers and corporate decline. Discover more from Tim at The Unshackled For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: BEN MAI
youtube.summary: Simon O’Connor speaks with Auckland Church Network’s Ben Mai about the return of the Nativity float to the Auckland Santa Parade, bringing the story of Christ’s birth back to an event that had gone around 15 years without a Christian presence. For further information: Visit the Auckland Church Network website or check out their Art Competition Donate to their Give a Little campaign

youtube.title: "Frog marched off the premises with a cardboard box." - RCR Co-Founder
youtube.summary: "Frog marched off the premises with a cardboard box." - RCR Co-Founder Alia Bland explains how the lasting hurt of Kiwis who lost their careers during the COVID years helped drive RCR's Vote Smart 2026 campaign. For those who felt abandoned and unheard, the campaign aimed to give them a political voice and keep Labour and the left bloc out of government. When politicians won't listen to the people they hurt, does the ballot box become the loudest voice of all? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/alia-bland-claire-deeks-founders-of-rcr-voices-for-freedom-did-billionaires-really-shape-the-election #RCRMedia

youtube.title: "The old belief that the base has nowhere else to go. What are they going to do?" - Professor Ramesh
youtube.summary: "The old belief that the base has nowhere else to go. What are they going to do?" - Professor Ramesh Thakur, Political Scholar & Former UN Official Professor Ramesh Thakur questions whether traditional political parties have taken their loyal voters for granted, pointing to growing support for smaller parties in New Zealand and populist movements overseas. Have the major parties spent so long assuming their voters would never leave that they've forgotten how to convince them to stay? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/ramesh-thakur-political-scholar-former-un-official-trust-in-democracy-is-crumbling-globally #RCRMedia

youtube.title: "That would seem to suggest that there is very little editorial supervision at all."
youtube.summary: "That would seem to suggest that there is very little editorial supervision at all." - David Harvey, Former Judge From disputed explanations of National's overhang to spelling mistakes and questionable editing, David Harvey questions the quality control behind mainstream news reporting. If the people explaining elections to the public can't get the details right, who exactly is checking the checkers? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/the-fourth-estate-with-david-harvey-media-bias-on-display-with-split-vote-reporting #RCRMedia #TheFourthEstate

youtube.title: Helen Clark went into the Coromandel and pleaded with everyone to vote for Jeanette Fitzsimons...
youtube.summary: "Helen Clark went into the Coromandel and pleaded with everyone to vote for Jeanette Fitzsimons with their candidate vote, not their party vote, and they did." - Maurice Williamson, Former NZ MP & Statistician Maurice Williamson fires back at critics of strategic voting, pointing to Helen Clark's support for Green candidate Jeanette Fitzsimons in Coromandel in 1999. If split voting was acceptable when it helped Labour and the Greens, why is the same strategy suddenly controversial when the centre-right uses it? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/maurice-williamson-former-nz-mp-statistician-strategic-voting-delivers-a-seismic-shift-in-the-election #RCRMedia

youtube.title: KIRRALIE SMITH
youtube.summary: Binary Australia director Kirralie Smith discusses the documentary Who Decides?, which examines disputes over sex-based rights in sport, education and healthcare. She argues that parents are losing authority over decisions affecting their children and calls for changes to the Sex Discrimination Act. Kirralie also outlines her ongoing legal battle over vilification findings, a $95,000 damages order and her campaign to restore biological sex protections in Australian law. For more information: Check out the film’s website ‘Who Decides’ or follow the film on Facebook , Instagram , X , TikTok , YouTube For more on Binary Australia

youtube.title: Tim Wilms chats with Lachlan Lade about the growing disconnect in Australian society.
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms chats with Lachlan Lade from the Australian Lobby Group about the growing disconnect in Australian society. Lade argues that shared national values, identity and allegiance to the Australian flag have been eroded. He criticises both major political parties, outlines the Australia Lobby Group’s push for major immigration restrictions and explains its campaign to mobilise Australians and hold politicians accountable for restoring national identity.

youtube.title: Tim Wilms talks with comedian and influencer Lisa Spencer about the Australia marches in Melbourne
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms catches up with comedian, writer and influencer Lisa Spencer to share her impressions of the Australia marches in Melbourne, describing a noticeably different energy and atmosphere from previous protests. They also discusses the approaching Victorian election, their opposition to another Labor government and hopes for political change in the state.

youtube.title: Tim Wilms talks with cartoonist and One Nation candidate Mark Nicholson
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms talks with cartoonist and One Nation candidate Mark Nicholson about the energy behind the party’s growing election campaign, and his decision to stand in Melbourne’s Northern Metropolitan Region. He also discusses continuing his political cartoons if elected and argues that One Nation is now offering practical solutions, pointing to its 63-page policy platform.

youtube.title: Tim Wilms speaks with One Nation candidate Michael Piastrino about why he left the Liberal Party
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms speaks with One Nation candidate Michael Piastrino about why he left the Liberal Party, accusing it of lacking backbone and failing to represent voters. He outlines One Nation’s ambitions to win seats across Melbourne’s south-east, promising to put local concerns first, including reversing the renaming of Berwick Springs Lake (which was recently named Guru Nanak Lake for the Indian community).

youtube.title: Tim Wilms speaks with founder of Turning Point Australia & Protect Our Kids Edward Schuller
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms speaks with founder of Turning Point Australia & Protect Our Kids Edward Schuller. They discusses efforts to challenge the influence of external organisations in school sex education, transgender ideology and what he describes as the growing bureaucratisation of education. Through the Protect Our Kids campaign, he is calling for these organisations to be removed from schools, their government funding cut and greater parental oversight restored.

youtube.title: He would've easily have shifted 100,000 votes. He wouldn't have lost an MP. He would have gained...
youtube.summary: "He would've easily have shifted 100,000 votes. He wouldn't have lost an MP. He would have gained four." - Rodney Hide, Former ACT Party Leader Rodney Hide argues that National could have benefited from embracing RCR's Vote Smart campaign rather than opposing it. His hypothetical MMP model shows a larger centre-right bloc without National losing any of its 42 electorate seats. Was National's disagreement with Vote Smart really about electoral mathematics, or about how power would be shared inside the coalition? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/wednesday-webinars-politics-the-election-hangover-what-happens-next #RCRMedia #WednesdayWebinar
